results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] so as to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Bar changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a mixed conformance picture across two distinct change events:

**1. Initial Deployment (CreateEndpoint — 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) — SATISFIES the control:**
The model registry entry (id: 4cda121c) shows the model package was approved at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. The CloudTrail CreateEndpoint event (id: 171df8b3) fired at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z — two hours *after* approval. This temporal ordering demonstrates that a change was documented in the registry, approval was obtained before deployment, and the deployment was gated on that approval. This satisfies CM-3(1) sub-requirements (a) document proposed changes, (b) request approval, (d) bar changes until approval is received, and (e) document all changes.

**2. Hotfix Update (UpdateEndpoint — 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z) — FAILS the control:**
The CloudTrail UpdateEndpoint event (id: 5a784f93) shows a hotfix deployment to the endpoint using config "churn-predictor-v1-hotfix" by the same IAM user. Critically, no corresponding model registry entry exists for this change — the only registry entry is for version 1 approved in December 2025. This means:
- The change was **not documented** in the model registry before deployment (violates sub-req a).
- No approval authority was informed or approval sought (violates sub-req b).
- The change was **not barred** pending approval (violates sub-req d).
- No automated notification of completion to designated personnel is evidenced (violates sub-req f).

The automated change-control mechanism (SageMaker Model Registry) was bypassed entirely for the hotfix. This is a significant gap — hotfixes and emergency changes are precisely the scenarios where change control is most critical and most often circumvented.
gaps: No registry entry exists for the hotfix endpoint config 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' — human attestation needed to determine whether an out-of-band approval process (e.g., ticketing system, email approval) was followed.

No evidence of automated notifications (CM-3(1)(f)) to designated personnel upon completion of either change — notification logs or SNS/EventBridge configurations were not retrievable via available collectors.
No evidence of a mechanism to highlight unapproved changes within an organization-defined time period (CM-3(1)(c)) — e.g., no Config rules or alerting on registry-bypass deployments.
Only one model package version is present in the registry; it is unclear whether additional versions were created and later deleted, or whether the hotfix was intentionally unregistered.
